greek: καὶ ἐποίησεν ἡ γῆ ἐν τοῖς ἑπτὰ ἔτεσιν τῆς εὐθηνίας δράγματα·
hint: In the seven years of plenty the land produces abundant harvests.

notes.text: δράγμα, as much as one can grasp, a handful, a sheaf: the land made sheaves. The Hebrew has liqmāṣîm, by handfuls, an adverbial phrase.

reading: and [[made|made, did, produced, created|ποιέω]] [[the earth|the earth, the land, the ground|γῆ]] [[in|within, inside of, and by means of|ἐν]] to the seven to years [[of the prosperity|of the prosperity and plenty, of the good condition, of the abundance, of the corn-supply|εὐθηνία]] [[as much as one can grasp|as much as one can grasp and handfuls and trusses, sheaves, uncut corn|δράγμα]];

greek: καὶ συνήγαγεν πάντα τὰ βρώματα τῶν ἑπτὰ ἐτῶν, ἐν οἷς ἦν ἡ εὐθηνία ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτου, καὶ ἔθηκεν τὰ βρώματα ἐν ταῖς πόλεσιν, βρώματα τῶν πεδίων τῆς πόλεως τῶν κύκλῳ αὐτῆς ἔθηκεν ἐν αὐτῇ.
hint: Joseph gathers the food of the seven years and stores each city's surrounding harvest within it.

notes.text: In which was the plenty. The Hebrew has ʾăšer hāyû, which were, and no word for plenty.
The article over an adverb: of the things round about the city, the plains around it.

greek: καὶ συνήγαγεν Ιωσηφ σῖτον ὡσεὶ τὴν ἄμμον τῆς θαλάσσης πολὺν σφόδρα, ἕως οὐκ ἠδύναντο ἀριθμῆσαι, οὐ γὰρ ἦν ἀριθμός.
hint: Joseph gathers grain like the sand of the sea, until it can no longer be counted.

notes.text: Until they were not able to count, plural. The Hebrew has ʿad kî-ḥādal lispōr, until he left off counting.
For there was no number: the negative with the imperfect of εἰμί.

greek: Τῷ δὲ Ιωσηφ ἐγένοντο υἱοὶ δύο πρὸ τοῦ ἐλθεῖν τὰ ἑπτὰ ἔτη τοῦ λιμοῦ, οὓς ἔτεκεν αὐτῷ Ασεννεθ θυγάτηρ Πετεφρη ἱερέως Ἡλίου πόλεως.
hint: Before the famine, Asenath bears Joseph two sons.

notes.text: The seven years of the famine. The Hebrew has šĕnat hārāʿāb, the year of the famine, with no number.
πρό with the genitive of the articular infinitive: before the coming.

greek: ἐκάλεσεν δὲ Ιωσηφ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ πρωτοτόκου Μανασση, ὅτι Ἐπιλαθέσθαι με ἐποίησεν ὁ θεὸς πάντων τῶν πόνων μου καὶ πάντων τῶν τοῦ πατρός μου.
hint: Joseph names his firstborn Manasseh, because God has made him forget his toil and his father's house.

notes.text: ποιέω with an infinitive: he made me to forget. The Hebrew name and its reason share a root, nāšâ; the Greek reason, ἐπιλανθάνομαι, does not sound like the name.
All the ones of my father, the article standing for its noun. The Hebrew has kol-bêt ʾābî, all my father's house.

names.gloss: (Μανασση, from Hebrew Mĕnaššeh, which the Hebrew hears in naššanî, "he made me forget")

greek: τὸ δὲ ὄνομα τοῦ δευτέρου ἐκάλεσεν Εφραιμ, ὅτι Ηὔξησέν με ὁ θεὸς ἐν γῇ ταπεινώσεώς μου.
hint: He names the second Ephraim, because God increased him in the land of his humiliation.

notes.text: αὐξάνω, to make large, increase. The Hebrew has hiprānî, he made me fruitful, the root the Hebrew hears in the name; the Greek verb does not echo it.

greek: Παρῆλθον δὲ τὰ ἑπτὰ ἔτη τῆς εὐθηνίας, ἃ ἐγένοντο ἐν γῇ Αἰγύπτῳ,
hint: The seven years of plenty in Egypt come to an end.

hint: The famine years begin as Joseph said; there is famine everywhere, but bread in Egypt.

notes.text: In all the earth, singular. The Hebrew has bĕkol-hāʾărāṣôt, in all the lands.

greek: καὶ ἐπείνασεν πᾶσα ἡ γῆ Αἰγύπτου, ἐκέκραξεν δὲ ὁ λαὸς πρὸς Φαραω περὶ ἄρτων· εἶπεν δὲ Φαραω πᾶσι τοῖς Αἰγυπτίοις Πορεύεσθε πρὸς Ιωσηφ, καὶ ὃ ἐὰν εἴπῃ ὑμῖν, ποιήσατε.
hint: When Egypt hungers and cries to Pharaoh, he sends the people to Joseph to do whatever he says.

notes.text: The reduplicated aorist of κράζω, to croak, scream, cry aloud.
Close in wording to John 2:5, ὅ τι ἂν λέγῃ ὑμῖν ποιήσατε.
To all the Egyptians; the Hebrew has lĕkol-miṣrayim, to all Egypt.

hint: The famine spreads over the land; Joseph opens the granaries and sells to the Egyptians.

notes.text: The granaries: LSJ's place for storing corn, granary, citing this verse; Middle Liddell has no entry. The Hebrew has kol-ʾăšer bāhem, all that was in them.
The imperfect: he kept selling. The Hebrew verse goes on, wayyeḥĕzaq hārāʿāb bĕʾereṣ miṣrāyim, and the famine grew strong in the land of Egypt; the Greek has no such clause.

hint: All countries come to Egypt to buy grain from Joseph, for the famine prevails everywhere.

notes.text: All the countries, plural; the Hebrew has kol-hāʾāreṣ, all the earth.
